hook.text: A company sells parts from its Irish subsidiary to its US parent at a price that shifts profit to the lower-tax country.

buildup.text: Transfer pricing is the price charged between divisions of the same company for goods or services moving across borders.

discovery.text: Companies use transfer pricing to allocate profits to lower-tax jurisdictions—legally reducing their global tax bill.

twist.text: Governments fight aggressive transfer pricing. The OECD's arm's-length principle says prices must match market rates.

climax.text: Apple faced a $14 billion EU tax ruling for routing profits through Ireland. Transfer pricing is under global scrutiny.

punchline.text: Move products across borders. Profits follow—and so do regulators.

quiz.question: What is transfer pricing?
options: Prices charged between divisions of the same company
